statements.t: As explained below, our rebranding initiative will eliminate or de-emphasize our reference to the sub-brands going forward.
By streamlining our global identity, we aim to strengthen customer recognition, enhance operational efficiency and better align to our customers’ needs with a singular, powerful brand narrative.
We believe this transformation will position Ultralife for ongoing growth and stronger market impact as we continue to lead in mission critical battery and RF power solutions.
We will provide copies of these reports upon written request to the attention of Philip A.

The Merger is expected to be effected pursuant to Section 251(h) of the Delaware General Corporation Law (the “DGCL”), without a vote of the Company’s stockholders, subject to the satisfaction or waiver of the applicable conditions set forth in the Merger Agreement.
The Company cannot assure that the conditions to the Offer and the Merger will be satisfied or waived or that the transactions will be completed within the anticipated timeframe or at all.

Following the Effective Time, the Company’s Shares are expected to be delisted from the Nasdaq Stock Market and deregistered under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (the “Exchange Act”), as soon as practicable and, in any event, within 10 days after the Closing Date.
The transaction is expected to result in a change in the Company’s ownership and governance structure.

The Company expects to recognize incremental stock based compensation expense in connection with the acceleration and settlement of outstanding equity awards, subject to the final determination of the applicable accounting treatment and the timing of the consummation of the transaction.

In addition, subject to the terms of the Merger Agreement, Covered Employees whose employment is involuntarily terminated without cause during the applicable continuation period will be entitled to severance payments and benefits on terms no less favorable than those under the Company’s existing severance policies immediately prior to the Effective Time.
In connection with the proposed transaction, the Company expects to incur transaction-related expenses, including legal, financial advisory, accounting and other professional fees.
The Company will continue to evaluate the appropriate classification and timing of such expenses as additional information becomes available.
The transaction consideration payable to the Company’s stockholders will be funded in accordance with the terms of the Merger Agreement and the arrangements made by Parent and Merger Sub.

The Company’s liquidity and capital resources prior to the consummation of the transaction will continue to be affected by its operating results, working capital requirements, capital expenditures, debt obligations and other ordinary-course business activities, as well as transaction-related expenses.
The Company will continue to monitor its liquidity and capital requirements throughout the pendency of the transaction.
The Company cannot assure that the transaction will be consummated or that the transaction will be completed within the anticipated timeframe.
If the transaction is not consummated, the Company may incur substantial transaction expenses without realizing the anticipated benefits of the transaction.
The Company expects to incur additional legal, financial advisory and other professional fees in connection with the transaction.

The Company’s future operating strategy, capital allocation and business plans following completion of the transaction will be determined in light of Parent’s plans and the circumstances existing at that time.

If the transaction is not consummated, the Company will continue to operate as an independent company, subject to the risks associated with its business, financial condition and operating environment, as well as the potential effects of the failed transaction.
The Company will continue to evaluate the transaction and its potential effects on the Company’s financial position, results of operations and liquidity as the transaction progresses.

For the three-month period ended September 30, 2026, Ultralife recognized an income tax provision of $362, comprised of a current tax provision of $67 and a deferred tax provision of $295 which primarily represents non-cash charges for U.S. taxes which we expect will be fully offset by net operating loss carryforwards and other tax credits for the foreseeable future.

The income tax provision for the first nine months of 2026 is comprised of a $148 current provision for taxes expected to be paid on income primarily in foreign jurisdictions and a $490 deferred tax provision which primarily represents non-cash charges for U.S. income taxes that we expect will be fully offset by net operating loss carryforwards and other tax credits for the foreseeable future.

For the comparable 2025 period, the income tax provision was comprised of a $182 current provision for taxes expected to be paid on income primarily in foreign jurisdictions and a $124 deferred tax provision which primarily represents non-cash charges for U.S. taxes that we expect will be fully offset by net operating loss carryforwards and other tax credits for the foreseeable future.

Management, including our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, does not expect that the Company’s disclosure controls and procedures or its internal control over financial reporting will prevent or detect all error and all fraud.
